ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the rhombus OABC has side OA on the x-axis, with point $A(10, 0)$, and $\sin\angle COA=\frac{4}{5}$. If the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}$ ($k>0, x>0$) passes through point C, what is the value of $k$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\[ \text{{\bfseries Solution:}} \text{ As shown in the figure, draw } CE \perp OA \text{ at point E,} \]
\[ \because \text{ the side OA of the rhombus OABC lies on the x-axis, with point } A(10,0), \]
\[ \therefore OC = OA = 10, \]
\[ \because \sin\angle COA = \frac{4}{5} = \frac{CE}{OC}, \]
\[ \therefore CE = 8, \]
\[ \therefore OE = \sqrt{CO^2 - CE^2} = 6, \]
\[ \therefore \text{ the coordinates of point C are }(6, 8), \]
\[ \because \text{ if the inverse ratio function } y = \frac{k}{x} (k>0, x>0) \text{ passes through point C,} \]
\[ \therefore k = 6 \times 8 = \boxed{48} \]

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a rectangular coordinate system, O is at the origin, OA is located on the positive x-axis, and point A is to the right of O; quadrilateral OABC is drawn as a rhombus, point C is in the first quadrant and OC inclines from O toward the upper right, so ∠COA is an acute angle. The figure also draws the inverse proportional function curve in the first quadrant, and it passes through point C. Reasoning: From A(10,0), it can be known that OA=10. Because OABC is a rhombus, the adjacent side OC=OA=10. Let θ=∠COA, and it is known that sinθ=4/5; also from the image it can be seen that θ is an acute angle, so cosθ=sqrt(1-(4/5)^2)=3/5. Thus the coordinates of point C are (10·cosθ, 10·sinθ)=(10·3/5,10·4/5)=(6,8). The inverse proportional function y=k/x passes through C(6,8); substituting gives 8=k/6, so k=6×8=48.
